bib.title: SkillGym: Internalizing Human Skills into LLMs for Real-World Problem Solving

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "SkillGym: Internalizing Large-Scale Human Skills into LLMs for Real-World Problem Solving". First author Zhilong Ge (ECNU and Shanghai AI Lab; Ge, Shao, Yang, Cai equal contribution; corresponding author Jie Zhou). Preprint arXiv:2609.27717v2 [cs.CL], dated 24 Sep 2026 (so September 2026). No venue.
COVERAGE: 22 of 22 pages read, 83,288 chars, including appendices A-D and Tables 6-11. Figure axes and chart glyphs are garbled. References were only skimmed.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. SFT on skill-derived trajectories lifts the Qwen3.5-35B-A3B base across all four metrics under both harnesses.
 number: Claude Code +199 Elo GDPval-AA v2, +19.10 pp Terminal-Bench 2.1, +28.13 and +14.68 pp SkillsBench with and without skills. Codex +37 Elo, +35.96, +27.69, +20.39.
 setup: SFT only, no RL. Full-parameter SFT on 16 H200 GPUs (ms-swift Megatron). Single trained checkpoint per harness. TB 2.1 is 89 tasks. SkillsBench v1.1 is 87 tasks. GDPval-AA v2 is 220 tasks. No seeds or variance reported (SkillsBench "targeting three trials" appears only in the description of public results).
 quote: "Under Claude Code, it gains 199 Elo on GDPval-AA v2 (974 to 1173) and 19.10 percentage points on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (39.33% to 58.43%)." p8
 where: Table 4, p8
2. Without skills at inference, the trained agent beats its skill-assisted base. This is the "internalization" claim.
 number: 26.81% vs 23.34% (Claude Code), 21.08% vs 5.33% (Codex)
 quote: "Notably, without inference-time skills, the trained agent exceeds its skill-assisted base under both Claude Code (26.81% versus 23.34%) and Codex (21.08% versus 5.33%)." p8
 Skills still help the trained agent, so the paper calls the two "complementary".
3. 35B model versus references and comparable-scale baselines.
 number: SkillsBench with skills 51.47% vs Sonnet 4.6 47.2, GPT-5.4 Mini 41.4, DeepSeek V4 Pro Preview 50.1. TB 2.1 58.43 vs Sonnet 58.5. Versus Agents-A1: +189 Elo, +14.61 pp TB, +21.18 and +13.44 SkillsBench.
 setup: reference scores are public and come from different harnesses (OpenHands, Terminus-2, Claude Code, and others), so they are not controlled. It does not reach the frontier models: GPT-5.4 TB 77.3, Opus 4.8 74.6.
 quote: "On skill-assisted SkillsBench, it reaches 51.47%, surpassing Claude Sonnet 4.6 (47.2%), GPT-5.4 Mini (41.4%), and DeepSeek V4 Pro (Preview) (50.1%)." p8
 Other 32B baselines (TerminalTraj, Nemotron-Terminal, OpenThinker-Agent) score 0 to 2.3% on SkillsBench, Table 11 p22.
4. Dataset: 2,756 environments, 12 categories, 63 sub-categories. 1,081 are skill-dependent (39.2%) and 1,675 verifier-passed fallback. There are 8,364 successful trajectories averaging 49.0 tool calls, 63.4k logged tokens and 35.2 steps (max 350 tool calls, 318 steps). Average build time is 4.5 h per task with GPT-5.4.
 quote: "Across 48,152 sampled trials, only 8,364 pass the outcome verifiers, yielding an overall success rate of 17.4%" p6
 Teachers: Claude Code with DeepSeek V4 Pro and GLM-5.2, Codex with GPT-5.4 and Nex-N2-Pro. Trajectories span 2,302 unique tasks. Only 36.8% of successful trajectories explicitly invoke the target skill (17.1% to 57.4% by config), Table 2 p6.
5. Ablation, teacher mixing (Table 5, p9). Mixing helps terminal and skill metrics but hurts GDPval.
 number: Codex: GPT-5.4 alone 24.72 TB, 14.00 SB, 6.96 SB-w/o. Nex alone 33.71, 13.59, 12.61. GPT+Nex 40.45, 19.91, 13.59. All teachers 46.07, 33.02, 21.08. Claude Code: DeepSeek alone 43.82 TB, GLM alone 55.06, DeepSeek+GLM 57.30, all 58.43. GDPval: Nex alone 1074 vs GPT+Nex 976, and GLM alone 1212 vs all-teacher 1173.
 quote: "these two-teacher mixtures reduce GDPval-AA v2 scores by 98 and 51 Elo relative to the strongest single-teacher students" p8
6. Ablation, harness pooling. Adding the other harness's trajectories improves Codex a lot (skill-assisted 19.91 to 33.02) but reduces Claude Code skill-free from 28.41 to 26.81.
 The authors concede it "does not isolate harness diversity from changes in teacher composition and data volume." p9
7. Contrastive skill-dependency filter: a task is Skill-Dep. if the reference agent passes with the skill and fails without it, (r+, r-) = (1,0). No ablation compares training on Skill-Dep. tasks against fallback tasks.

LIMITS
- No RL was run. Conclusion: "Future work will explore reinforcement learning in our task environments, using verifier-derived outcome rewards". The "RL environment" framing is a promise, not a result. Rewards are binary, code-verifier outcomes, r in {0,1}, Eq. 3.
- Codex comparison confounded: base uses the standard system prompt, the trained agent uses the no-applypatch prompt, so "its performance difference cannot be attributed solely to fine-tuning" (p22).
- Public reference scores come from mixed harnesses and are not controlled. DeepSeek V4 Pro SkillsBench is the preview checkpoint.
- Skill dependence is "evidence under the reference configuration, not proof that the skill is necessary".
- Verifiers check task requirements, not output quality. Anti-shortcut checks exist (tamper, answer-copying, fabricated outputs).
- Only successful trajectories were used for SFT, and 17.4% pass. Teachers are strong proprietary or open models, so this is distillation, not self-improvement.
- Single run per cell, no confidence intervals. No ablation on data size or on skill-dependent versus fallback data. Only one student model, 35B-A3B.
- Task templates are manually built per sub-category. Skills come from the ClawHub registry (high-star skills).
- Coverage is uneven: nosql-databases has 1 task, culinary-arts has 0 successful trajectories.

BUILDS ON: Voyager (Wang et al., 2023), AutoSkill (Yang et al., 2026), Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023), Anthropic agent skills (2025), OpenClaw/ClawHub (2026), CodeRL (Le et al., 2022), DeepSeekMath (Shao et al., 2024), DeepSeek-R1 (Guo et al., 2025), ToolBench/ToolLLM (Qin et al., 2024), TerminalTraj, Nemotron-Terminal (Pi et al., 2026), OpenThoughts-Agent (Raoof et al., 2026), Agents-A1 (Bai et al., 2026). Benchmarks: SkillsBench (Li et al., 2026), Terminal-Bench (Merrill et al., 2026), GDPval (Patwardhan et al., 2025).

BEARS ON YOUR NOTES
- Note 05 ("learning without weights first", SkillRL): this is the weights-side counterpart. Skills in context are a baseline, and SFT moves the with-skill and without-skill scores. It shows skills and weights are complementary (trained agent still gains from skills). It does not compare against a skills-in-context-only method like SkillRL at matched cost.
- Note 06 (data and environments): the strongest fit. It covers the pipeline (templates, Docker, verifier, two-level acceptance, contrastive test), yield (17.4% trajectory success, 4.5 h build per task) and teacher-mixing ablation.
- Note 07 (reward design): binary code-verifier outcome rewards with anti-shortcut checks. Only designed, not trained. Do not cite this as an RL result.

CODE: none. Eq. 1-3 are in the text: E_i = (x_i, A_i, rho_i, V_i), the label rule on p4, and r = V_i(z(tau)) in {0,1}.

FIGURES: Fig 1 (p2) bar charts of Table 11 results against baselines and frontier references. Fig 2 (p3) pipeline: A skill cards and templates, B Docker environment, feasibility and skill-dependency test, C multi-harness sampling. Fig 3 (p13) category breakdown. I did not run the figure-caption script.

PROBLEMS: Chart glyphs in Figs 4-6 are garbled and carry no data. No embedded instructions found. Dates are as printed (a 2026 preprint citing models such as GPT-5.4 and Claude Opus 4.8). I could not verify the cited benchmark numbers against their sources.
